content.value_statement: Creator deals fail when deliverables, rights, payment, and approvals stay vague. This skill turns agreed terms into contract drafts, review memos, clause explanations, and negotiation points.
actual_capabilities: Collects parties, deliverables, compensation, platform, usage-rights, exclusivity, approval, and disclosure inputs.
Drafts an influencer agreement framework covering scope, payment, ownership, compliance, warranties, confidentiality, termination, and signatures.
Reviews incoming agency or creator terms against essential clauses and red-flag checks.
Explains key contract clauses with practical watch-outs for brands and creators.
Produces negotiation ranges for usage rights, exclusivity, revisions, payment, and whitelisting.
limitations: It provides general contract guidance, not legal advice or attorney review.
It depends on the user supplying accurate deal terms and jurisdiction details.
It does not negotiate with creators or agencies before commercial terms exist.
It does not execute signatures or connect to external systems without optional tooling.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Brand Campaign Agreement
use_cases.description: Turn approved creator terms into a structured draft with deliverables, payment schedule, disclosure duties, and licensed content rights.

use_cases.title: Review Incoming Agency Paper
use_cases.description: Check a pasted agreement for missing essentials, broad exclusivity, perpetual rights, delayed payment, and unclear approval terms.

use_cases.title: Create a Reusable Deal Template
use_cases.description: Build a repeatable contract checklist and clause set for common creator collaborations before final legal review.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Simple Agreement
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner draft from basic commercial terms.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an influencer agreement for one creator. Deliverables are [deliverables]. Compensation is [amount and timing]. Platform is [platform]. Use basic owned-channel usage rights and include FTC disclosure language.

prompt_templates.title: Fill Contract Parameters
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me gather the missing contract parameters for this creator deal: [brief]. Ask only for missing parties, deliverables, timeline, compensation, usage rights, exclusivity, approval, and platform details.

prompt_templates.title: Review Agency Terms
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of pasted agreement terms.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these influencer agreement terms and identify missing essentials, red flags, and negotiation points. Focus on payment timing, usage rights, whitelisting, exclusivity, revisions, approval, termination, and disclosure duties: [paste terms].

prompt_templates.title: Build Negotiation Positions
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a negotiation cheat sheet for this creator contract. Compare each open term with standard ranges, propose a brand position, a creator-friendly fallback, and terms that require legal review: [deal terms].

output_examples.input: Draft a simple agreement for two Instagram posts at $500.
output_examples.output: A streamlined agreement with two post deliverables, a $500 payment schedule, 12-month owned-channel usage rights, disclosure requirements, and a short timeline.

output_examples.input: Review terms asking for perpetual paid usage and six months of category exclusivity.
output_examples.output: A review memo flags broad usage and exclusivity as negotiation issues, suggests paid whitelisting terms, and recommends narrower category language.

output_examples.input: Explain the usage-rights clause to a campaign manager.
output_examples.output: A plain-language clause explanation covers permitted channels, duration, territory, modifications, paid amplification, and when extra creator compensation is typical.

best_practices: Provide final business terms before drafting so the agreement does not guess core obligations.
Separate organic repost rights from paid amplification and whitelisting rights.
Send significant or unusual contracts to qualified legal counsel before signature.
anti_patterns: Using perpetual usage rights as the default for small creator deals.
Leaving deliverables, deadlines, or approval standards vague.
Treating the generated template as a substitute for legal review.

faq.question: Does this skill provide legal advice?
faq.answer: No. It provides general contract guidance and templates. A qualified lawyer should review contracts before execution.

faq.question: Can it review a contract from an agency?
faq.answer: Yes. Paste the terms and it checks essentials, red flags, and negotiation points.

faq.question: What deal terms should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide parties, deliverables, dates, compensation, platforms, approval process, usage rights, exclusivity, and disclosure needs.

faq.question: Does it handle FTC disclosure requirements?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes disclosure prompts and compliance language for sponsored creator content.

faq.question: Can it draft whitelisting or paid amplification terms?
faq.answer: Yes. It can define paid social permissions, duration, platform scope, and additional compensation prompts.

faq.question: Can it sign or send the agreement?
faq.answer: No. It can prepare the terms. E-signature routing requires separate tools or manual workflow.
